{{short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=August 2023}} {{Infobox NCAA team season |mode=Basketball |year=2019–20 |team=Nevada Wolf Pack |image=Nevada Wolf Pack wordmark.svg |image_size=150 |conference=Mountain West Conference |short_conf=MW |CoachRank= |APRank= |record=19–12 |conf_record=12–6 |head_coach=[[Steve Alford]] |hc_year = 1st |assoc_coach=[[Craig Neal]] |ahc_year = 1st |asst_coach1=Kory Barnett (1st season) |asst_coach2=Bill Duany (1st season) |stadium=[[Lawlor Events Center]] |champion=[[Paradise Jam tournament]] champions |bowl= |bowl_result= }} {{2019–20 Mountain West Conference men's basketball standings}} The '''2019–20 Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Nevada, Reno]] during the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Wolf Pack, led by first-year head coach [[Steve Alford]], played their home games at the [[Lawlor Events Center]] on their campus in [[Reno, Nevada]] as members of the [[Mountain West Conference]] (MW). They finished the season 19–12, 12–6 in Mountain West play to finish in a three-way tie for second place. They lost in the quarterfinals of the [[2020 Mountain West Conference men's basketball tournament|Mountain West tournament]] to [[2019–20 Wyoming Cowboys basketball team|Wyoming]]. ==Previous season== The [[2018–19 Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball team|Wolf Pack]] finished the season 29–5, 15–3 in Mountain West play to share the regular season Mountain West championship with [[2018–19 Utah State Aggies men's basketball team|Utah State]]. They defeated [[2018–19 Boise State Broncos men's basketball team|Boise State]] in the quarterfinals of the [[2019 Mountain West Conference men's basketball tournament|Mountain West tournament]] before losing in the semifinals to [[2018–19 San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball team|San Diego State]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they lost in the first round to [[2018–19 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]].{{Cite web|url=https://bustingbrackets.com/2019/09/14/nevada-basketball-2019-20-season-preview-wolf-pack/|title=Nevada Basketball: 2019-20 season preview for Wolf Pack|date=2019-09-14|website=Busting Brackets|language=en-US|access-date=2019-11-08}} On April 7, head coach Eric Musselman resigned to become the head coach at [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/26462667/arkansas-hires-nevada-musselman-coach|title = Arkansas hires Nevada's Musselman as coach|date = 7 April 2019}} He finished at Nevada with a four-year record of 110–34, three trips to the NCAA Tournament, and were champions of the [[2016 College Basketball Invitational]]. On April 11, Nevada hired [[Steve Alford]] as their next head coach.{{Cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/26501450/ex-ucla-coach-alford-hired-lead-nevada|title=Ex-UCLA coach Alford hired to lead Nevada|date=12 April 2019}} ==Offseason== ===Departures=== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" !
